name: Tuckerman Ravine Trail
quote: climbs steadily to Hermit Lake Shelters (2.4 miles, 1800 feet elevation gain)
why: Climb from Pinkham Notch to the Hermit Lake Shelters below Tuckerman Ravine on Mt. Washington; 2.4 mi one-way doubled. The page gives no distance to the summit, so this covers only the Hermit Lake section.

name: Welch-Dickey Loop Trail
quote: continuing over the summits of both Welch and Dickey mountains over 4.4 miles
why: Loop over the open ledges of Welch and Dickey mountains near Waterville Valley.

name: Piper Trail
quote: The Piper Trail is a challenging trail that summits Mt. Chocorua (3,500 ft.) in 4.3 miles and 2,700 ft. of elevation gain.
why: Challenging out-and-back to the bare summit of Mt. Chocorua; 4.3 mi one-way doubled.

name: Carter Ledge Trail
quote: the Carter Ledge Trail is a strenuous 4.5 mile hike to the summit of Mt. Chocorua
why: Strenuous route from White Ledge Campground to the summit of Mt. Chocorua; 4.5 mi to the summit, doubled.

name: Mt. Osceola (Osceola Trailhead)
quote: The trail reaches the summit of Mt. Osceola in 3.2 miles with excellent views.
why: Out-and-back from Tripoli Road to the 4,000-footer Mt. Osceola; 3.2 mi one-way doubled.

name: Baldface Circle Trail
quote: the Baldface Circle Trail, which provides a 9 mile loop over North and South Baldface summits
why: Long loop over the open North and South Baldface summits, passing Emerald Pool.

name: Webster - Jackson Trail
quote: can be hiked as a 6.5 mile loop using the Webster Cliff Trail to connect the two summits
why: Crawford Notch loop over Mt. Webster and Mt. Jackson.

name: Signal Ridge Trail (Mt. Carrigain)
quote: It is a 5 mile hike up the Signal Ridge Trail to the tower
why: Climb to the observation tower on Mt. Carrigain; 5 mi up, doubled.

name: Mousilauke Carriage Road
quote: The historic Mousilauke Carriage Road ascends to the summit Mt. Moosilauke in 5.1 miles.
why: Historic carriage road to the alpine summit of Mt. Moosilauke; 5.1 mi one-way doubled. The page spells it 'Mousilauke'.

name: White Ledge Loop
quote: White Ledge Loop is a 4.4 mile loop trail to White Ledge (2,010 ft.); a 1,450 feet elevation gain.
why: Loop to the White Ledge viewpoint near Conway. The White Ledge Campground page calls it 'a moderate 4 mile loop'.

name: Mt. Tremont (Mt. Tremont Trailhead)
quote: The summit of Mt. Tremont (3,371 ft.) is reached in 2.8 miles, gaining 2,551 feet of elevation.
why: Steep climb from US 302 to the summit of Mt. Tremont; 2.8 mi one-way doubled.

name: Mount Kearsage (Kearsarge North Trailhead)
quote: Mount Kearsage (3,268ft.) can be summited using this approach in 3.1 miles and 2600 ft. of elevation gain.
why: Climb to the fire tower summit of Kearsarge North; 3.1 mi one-way doubled. 'Kearsage' is the page's spelling.

name: Three Ponds loop (Three Ponds Trailhead)
quote: an easy to moderate 5.3 mile loop back to the trailhead is possible via Donkey Hill Cut-off and the Kineo Trail
why: Easy-to-moderate loop past the Three Ponds shelter. The shorter option is 'an easy 2.2 mile walk' to the middle pond, one-way.

name: Hale Brook trail
quote: The trail ascends 2.2 miles to the summit of Mt. Hale and a connection with the Lend-A-Hand trail.
why: Short climb from Zealand Road to the summit of Mt. Hale; 2.2 mi one-way doubled.

name: Mt. Tecumseh (Mt Tecumseh Trailhead)
quote: The trail ascends Mt. Tecumseh, with good limited views from the summit at 2.5 mils.
why: Climb from Waterville Valley to the 4,000-footer Mt. Tecumseh; 2.5 mi to the summit, doubled. 'mils' [sic].

name: Wentworth Trail (Mt. Israel)
quote: reaches the summit of Mt. Israel (2,630 ft.) in 2.1 miles and 1,700 ft of elevation gain.
why: Climb from the Mead Base Conservation Center to the summit of Mt. Israel; 2.1 mi one-way doubled.

name: Moat Mountain (South Moat Mountain Trailhead)
quote: South Moat Mountain (2,770 ft.) can be reached in 2.7 miles from this trailhead
why: Climb near Conway to the open summit of South Moat Mountain; 2.7 mi one-way doubled. The quote is from the Saco district listing summary.

name: Snow's Mountain loop
quote: The trailhead accesses a 3.9 mile loop over Snow's Mountain with limited fine views.
why: Loop over Snow's Mountain in Waterville Valley.

name: Stinson Mountain Trail
quote: The Stinson Mountain Trail leaves from here and ascends 1.8 miles to Stinson Mt.
why: Short climb near Rumney to the summit of Stinson Mountain; 1.8 mi one-way doubled.

name: Black Mountain (Chippewa Trailhead)
quote: ascends the rocky summit of Black Mountain in 1.8 miles
why: Short climb to the rocky summit of Black Mountain; 1.8 mi one-way doubled. The quote is from the hiking listing summary.

name: Iron Mountain (Iron Mtn Trailhead)
quote: accesses Iron Mountain summit (2,726 ft.) in just 0.9 miles and 800 feet of elevation gain
why: Short, steep climb near Jackson to the Iron Mountain summit; 0.9 mi one-way doubled. The south cliffs are 0.7 mi farther.

name: Discovery Trail
quote: This 1.4 mile loop trail offers a living classroom in forest ecology.
why: Interpretive forest-ecology loop off the Kancamagus Highway.
